scope.description: Whole gnuplot application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: 2D/3D scientific plotting, plot types, functions, styling, axes, multiplots, terminals and interactive exploration.

coverage.rationale: Explicit asymmetric lower/upper envelopes and captured typed-CSV handoffs deepen the bounded 2D publication family. Most plot types, 3D, composition, functions, rich styling and interactive exploration remain absent, so the coarse whole-application estimate stays at 20%.

scope.description: Named numeric CSV series with declared units, explicit ranges, symmetric y intervals or one supplied asymmetric range envelope to independently checked SVG/PNG.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Series, unit and supplied-bound intent hide plotting scripts and native filled-curve geometry. Authors still choose columns, ranges, compatible scales and the meaning of supplied bounds; the existing 70% estimate is retained within this bounded plotting family.

limitations: One to four ordinary numeric series or one asymmetric envelope on linear axes, with bounded tables and ASCII labels. No missing values, general functions, multiplots, arbitrary plot commands or inference of quantiles/confidence/coverage.

Every SVG bound vertex is checked. PNG verification samples interiors at each row and midpoint and exteriors where observable, requiring at least one across the plot; it is not full raster equivalence. Conservative pixel-clearance rules refuse some legitimate thin, steep or near-border envelopes.
The legend swatch and label have checked relative geometry; their pair is only constrained to the visible key row. Other label lengths have not been separately qualified in the isolated band proof.
A captured file or table artifact is still parsed against the explicit header, finite numeric rows, units and range contract; kind alone does not establish compatible CSV.
Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive native API measurement. Native availability, observed runtimes and source-bound qualification remain independent of both strength scores.
